quest.title: The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears
quest.description: To help Jeht find the Eternal Oasis, you must first find a Jinni who knows about the ancient past. It is said that this ruined temple plays host to just such a being...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Go to the temple on the outskirts of Gurabad

dialogues.speaker: Afiyah Chief's Hand-Written Orders
dialogues.text: "Make camp upon reaching your destination and seal the canyon to outsiders. Only members of the Tanit and the following tribes may pass..."

dialogues.speaker: Afiyah Chief's Hand-Written Orders
dialogues.text: "...If you discover any who carry a Jinni bottle with them, take it. The bounty will be split as agreed..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so they intentionally didn't go for Jeht, then?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...How interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Now, my master, we need not be hasty. Let us clear the next camp first.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You done, Azariq? You've bound your head up so tight that even Al-Ahmar himself would have trouble peeling your skin off! Who knows, he might even laugh at you for being a scaredy-cat!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hah. Is that how you talk to your elders, little wildcat? Have you forgotten your actual business here? Or about how someone's been waiting for you for half a day?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, and "someone" tanning themselves in the sun and having a drink or two passes for "business" now, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hmph. Woe to thieves who make false accusations! Just you watch: maybe I'll stick that clever little head of yours upside down in the sand. Maybe that'll clear it!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Rubbish, you haven't beaten me ever since you taught me how to wrestle.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You two get along so well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we've never seen two people start slinging mud at each other the moment they meet quite like you do...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha! Well, this is Azariq, a senior of mine in the tribe. He's like my older brother, and he's been a big help!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yes, yes, she treats me like a brother. And we'd get along better still, if she didn't like hanging out with the ladies more!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#And so what? Do you have a problem with that?}{F#Hey, hey, quit it! Stop giving them the wrong idea!}

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #Alright, whatever... {NICKNAME}, was it? Take care of her for me, eh? She's pretty good, but she likes charging into danger like a wildcat.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What was that? Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think you just said something bad about me!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: You'll see. Oh, you'll see.

choices.text: Okay, I think I get the gist of things...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hehe, don't you fret, {NICKNAME}'s a real experienced adventurer! Things will be fine here with Jeht. Just leave it to us!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What am I, a child?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hahahaha! *cough* Alright, alright, let's talk business.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Matriarch Babel has asked me to guide you into these city ruins. I'll lead the way, so follow closely.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so that's what it was. That's the first we've heard of what we need to do all day!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well, it wasn't all that convenient to explain our objective back at the settlement. The Matriarch believes the walls have ears.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Our objective here is to find the fragment of the Mother of the Jinn. We need it in order to be accepted into the Eternal Oasis at the desert's heart.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: The Jinn were the familiars of the Queen of All Oases, so it will naturally accept their presence. Their powers were also intended to create fertile lands amidst barren sands.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: So we... Well, Matriarch Babel, needs the aid of the Jinni to restore fertility to our tribe's soil, which will maintain the health of our herds.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Also, this particular Jinni still maintains her intelligence, so we should be able to pass through the seals on the Eternal Oasis with her aid.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yup, what he said.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Alright, that's that. To enter the ruins, we need to handle these mysterious devices first...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: For example, this one seems to be able to blow sand away in a specific direction... Although I'd call it something more akin to "breaking a seal," really...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Whatever the case, even though the method to unlock them has been lost, some trial and error on my part has shown that heavy impact can change the direction it's facing, creating runes that flow.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That should rid us of those annoying piles of sand.

talks.objective: Activate the device and open the gate
Activate the device and open the gate

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, why did you stop us? The thing we're looking for is just up ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Shh!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Look behind you — we're not alone.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: The temple's safe. I don't see any enemies, monsters, or dangerous devices.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: There's just this big thing... Heh. How interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: According to archaeological records left by people who came before us, as well as a stone slate that Aderfi got from within some ruins...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: This big object over here is the main device that keeps the Mother of the Jinn sealed.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Just from basic observation, I'd say that it's connected to the machine next to it. Perhaps they can be made to move in tandem somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... So we'll need to unlock this one by the side here to move the big object in the middle...?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: That's about right, I think. As for what happens afterward... I think we'll just have to cross that river when we get there.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Funny, I don't see any rivers.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Oh, knock it off, Jeht.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: So, I think we just need to repeat what we did at the gate... Let's crack this device open, shall we?

talks.objective: Activate the device within the temple

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, the machine has started, and the sand pile is gone... But the main device hasn't responded at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Did it not work?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #Wait, {NICKNAME}. You're the only one here who can use the elements, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm...?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Well, what I mean to say is that unlike us, who need to borrow the power of ancient spirits, your elemental abilities are innate, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah, that is the case.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what about it?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Why don't you try touching this big thing over here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... But... What if it turns out to be super dangerous?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You say that... But we should be careful all the same!

choices.text: We've touched all kinds of crazy things in the past, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: The records I've seen tell me that neither the mercenaries who came here nor those who used man-made Delusions were able to activate this device. But if you were to try...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you say "Delusions"...?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Huh? Did I? Think you might need to clean your ears a little... the desert winds carry sand into them a lot, so I hear.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I've got your back!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Or so I say, but you should be careful all the same. Just tell me if you think that something's amiss!

talks.objective: Touch the giant device at the temple's center

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Is the conversation with Matriarch Babel over?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: In that case... Let's take a short break.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hah, that's what I thought... Looks like the device earlier smoothed out its charging... uh, circuits? Looks like it's showing us the location of three other devices, too.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: I suppose that if we go to these devices, we'll be able to activate all four of these seal-breaking machines and clear the sand piles in front of us...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Aye, I think that's how it is... judging from my previous ruin-delving experiences, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! You sure do know a lot... and here Paimon thought you were just some guy in a tribe somewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey, hey, give the man some respect, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Oh! ... Sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hahaha, what do you even mean by that, Paimon? I'm a tribeswoman myself!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. Enough chit-chat. Let's follow the directions we've been given and look for the other three devices.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let me think. Let's start here.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: How do you know that we need to go this way first?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Haha. A desert dweller's intuition, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmph... If we get lost, it's on your head!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Relax. Both of us are here. If things go bad, we can fight our way out... or flee to safety.

talks.objective: Activate the device and, in turn, another machine somewhere within the temple

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: You can try changing the direction it's facing by hitting it. I think we can create runes that flow and thus clear the sand pile blocking our path.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Why am I not doing it, you ask? Haha, sorry, but we tribespeople have some taboos about this mysterious stuff... Can't be too careful and such...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Is there some problem?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hmph... I did see this large device in some really old theses, but this is the first time I've ever seen a real one up close.

dialogues.speaker: Neat Note
dialogues.text: "...The outland traveler may be identified by: their golden hair and eyes, strange foreign clothing, and a small floating fairy by their side..."

dialogues.speaker: Neat Note
dialogues.text: "...If they have obtained a Jinni, take it from them, and if they have yet to, then dispose of them..."

dialogues.speaker: Neat Note
dialogues.text: "Contact: Aderfi..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So it was Aderfi...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Someone you know, then?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My master, if I may, I would advise that you review your choice of friends. We had an old saying for this ilk...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: "The only loyal desert-dweller is one whose shoulders have been pierced by iron loops."

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: We should be rid of all of them now. Let us return.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: A lot of the ruined areas we've encountered on the way show signs of man-made damage... There might have been unrest here, or even a war.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: I'm no researcher, so I can't really read any pattern in these markings, but I doubt that the fate of this temple was a peaceful one.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: The books say that Gurabad was destroyed with searing fire and the great anger of the Jinn...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: The Jinn? Perhaps... But it looks more like the work of a mob, soldiers, or perhaps even tribespeople like us... But who knows, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But we can think about that later. I think this big guy here is our more pressing concern, no?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Indeed... Perhaps the other chambers are all structured like this one. Let's look around again, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll mark our path.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Mark? Paimon didn't see you do that.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We use scented oils made from Wenut larvae, planting it to mark the path we must tread, so that if we do get lost, we can just follow our nose to find the way back.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Now I'll have you know that our wildcat's nose is very sharp. We hunters wouldn't get very far without her!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Stop saying all that stuff, Azariq!

choices.text: That's right, you blockhead, stop bullying our little wildcat.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: And you! Don't you start with that nonsense too!

choices.text: Look, her fur's standing on end.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: It's not!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well, it's the... larva of a Wenut. *sigh* Agh, I've seen them so often that I'm actually not sure how to explain what they are. Tell you what, I'll explain more on the way back...

talks.objective: Scatter the dust around the sealing machine
Activate the device and, in turn, another machine somewhere within the temple

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Alright then. Go touch the device in the middle of the temple. Jeht and I will make sure you're safe.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Right, {NICKNAME}. Be careful now.

talks.objective: Look for a way back to the temple

Look for a way back to the temple

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Are you all alright?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Y—Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks. I'm alright.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That's good, that's good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew. That gave Paimon quite a fright...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: ...That tremor's source should be to the north, outside the temple.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah, I sensed that too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, why couldn't Paimon tell?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, that's true... Well, it's not like flying doesn't come with its own troubles, y'know?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #Let's go have a look, {NICKNAME}. Something huge is bound to have happened!

choices.text: You don't have much experience living in the desert, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true... But wait. You don't either!

talks.objective: Check on the situation outside the temple

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Have a look at this!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That's right. More ruins!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: A plaza with sides of seemingly equal length... and a new door's opened up on the opposite cliff. Is that our destination?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That's for you to explore, I fear.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Eh? Aren't you coming with us?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Sorry, but Matriarch Babel only asked me to open the way for you. You'll have to embark on the rest of the road yourself.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: I trust that you can protect your friends, right, Jeht?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, stop with that, you. What are you, my dad?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I know... Stay safe while you're heading back, you hear me?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: #Of course. {NICKNAME}, you take care of Jeht as well!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Why's Azariq just up and leaving on us like that? Isn't he gonna go deeper into the ruins with us?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: He's gone as deep as he wants to go, I think. These ruins are a cursed, taboo place to us Tanit... and the tribe's quite sensitive about that sort of thing.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But since I count as "half-outsider," I've got no qualms about going further. And anyway, you can't expect me to let you guys down!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you did ask us to help you find this Oasis thingamajiggie anyway, right? We're with you to the end!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, thanks!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yup. Don't worry, I'll watch your back for sure!

choices.text: We've only got each other from here on out.
So this was beneath the desert all the while...

talks.objective: Go to the ruins opposite the square

dialogues.text: Ah, Jeht! And our guests! So you are here, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: "After all"? You trying to get familiar with us? We're pretty busy over here, so you'd better have had a good reason to stop us.

dialogues.speaker: Messenger
dialogues.text: Ah, um... No, well, this... I was sent by Matriarch Babel with a message for you, Jeht. She has something urgent to discuss and would like you to, um... well, return to the campsite first...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This... That... What's got your tongue? Do you need me to shorten it for you? Did she say anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Messenger
dialogues.text: She'd like to speak with you alone... Sorry. I didn't know you were in a bad mood...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: A bad mood? Nonsense, I've never been better! You know, what with having found the Mother of the Jinn and all — which I'll be telling the Matriarch, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #I'm more than pleased, and so will she be, I bet! And so will her "master," to have a nice new servant — wouldn't you say, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Matriarch Babel has business with me, so I'll take my leave now. My deepest apologies for not serving you to the end, {M#Prince}{F#Princess} {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Alright, let's go see the Matriarch.

dialogues.speaker: Messenger
dialogues.text: S... Sure. As for you, honored guests, just follow this canyon, and you'll reach our camp soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Not much. I just thought that this child is quite interesting, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really, though, she's got quite the temper...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She isn't... y'know, jealous of a bottle, is she?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: You mean to say that she takes "a bottle" for her yardstick? Hah, perhaps.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Regardless, she is a good child. Trustworthy... if a little foolish.

choices.text: Stop talking about her like that. She's our friend.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah, see, I like you more already, my master.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Coming from you, that's kinda scary...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Oh, do not mistake my meaning, my master. I very much love the earnest impulsiveness of young women...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: But she will be taught, my dear master... Trust me, she will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if that happens, we'll pull her right outta the fire! That's what friends are for, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... The plants here have all withered... This doesn't look good.
No doubt, no doubt... And who shall we blame for that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Eh!? {NICKNAME}, Look! This bottle can talk!
You obstreperous oaf... Where did you get that active yet actively useless tongue of yours, I wonder?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eeek!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you... the Mother of the Jinn?
"Jinn"? Why, yes, I do count as one. "Mother"? Hmm... Well, if it does not displease you, I have been such before.
But "Mother of the Jinn"? Do those desert philistines wish to cajole me to laughter? I fear that this joke fails to amuse. It falls far short, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We have come on behalf of the Tanit tribe to see you, to ask that you show forth your great might and aid us in finding the place where Nabu Malikata slumbers...
Ah, so it is one of the desert folk. I like you, girl... You know the rules, and your manner of speech tickles me. Yes, you do amuse me.
Ah, but... Step aside for a moment. I shall have words with your lord only.
Mmm... The scent of unknown spices from afar... A servant girl of the desert-kin, and a flying pet...
#You must be a {M#Prince}{F#Princess} in exile, are you not?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Liloupar. Call me Liloupar.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Lilou... par... Wait a moment! You're... You're the one from the books...!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Speak not out of turn before your liege, sand-licking lackey!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She's my friend!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Jeht isn't a lackey! You're too much!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah. Is that so? Oh, the tedium...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah... If my soul were not sundered into many parts, unable to muster sufficient strength... I could shift into any number of shapes that might please you.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: A dancing girl, a lovely youth, an arhat or a yaksha... Or a lovely beast of those races that died out under the moon's light... I have been them all, and played all their parts, all for my lord's pleasure...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Your "lord"...?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: A lord I was willing to entrust my true name to... Yes, I did once have such a master. And today, I seem to have encountered his shadow.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You mean... Wait, wait a moment!

choices.text: I didn't understand you at all.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: She means that... Um, well, Jinn make contracts with humans by giving them their "true name." That name can be used to control the Jinn as one wills.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Huh. A learned desert dweller? Your servant girl is quite the rare find.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But those who strike such pacts... will eventually suffer the fearful vengeance of the Jinn, for the Jinn are a race that hates humanity.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hah! "Hate," you say? Such a strong word!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so what Jeht said is wrong?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Look at it this way: would you hate a poisonous insect or toad?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...And her name is Liloupar, which is the exact same name as the wicked spirit who drowned Ormazd, the mortal king of Gurabad, and his entire household in honey...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The history of Gurabad thereafter has been shrouded in dark secrets... Well, that's what I read, anyway.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But I don't get it. Is the one Babel looking for really such a dangerous figure?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ooh, a mighty interesting story that is... Is that how I am portrayed in your legends, then?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Are you worried that in making a contract with me, your lord... friend shall come to harm?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: But do you not wish to reach the place where Nabu Malikata slumbers? Hehehe... I shall not aid you, girl, or your... "Matriarch."

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I have no interest in your games of governance, nor shall I take part in your schemes... But your friend I shall serve, and give my true name.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #But... Why are you willing to give {NICKNAME} your true name, then? You must have a reason for that.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: #{M#Why, because I like him.}{F#Why, because I like her.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh!? Well, {NICKNAME} is plenty likable, sure...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: #Is it so strange? I like {M#him}{F#her} for {M#his}{F#her} scent, and also for {M#his}{F#her} choice in servants and pets... Yes, such taste truly is fitting of a {M#prince}{F#princess}.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Alright, I shan't speak more than I should. Come, Your Highness. Are you ready?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Servants and pets... Wait, do you mean Jeht and Paimon!? Gah! You're... so rude!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks you're right, Jeht! There's definitely something fishy with this thing. Let's just throw it away and...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I get the feeling that we should...

choices.text: For a friend, this is a trivial risk.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But... you...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: No, never mind... If this is your decision...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah... You are so very cute.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Well then, Your Highness, place me by your ear, and allow me to tell you my true name...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry about me.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...If you say so.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Do as Liloupar says.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text:
You place the magic bottle next to your ear.
You hear a soft chuckle, and then someone whispers something of unspeakable elegance and gentleness into that ear...
You are told of things as unknowable as the night wind, but you understand every last word nonetheless.
Then, the voice fades, and you feel something cold on your auricle...
Like a viper's kiss.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And with that, we are bound. I shall defend you, my master, from the encroachment of the desert, the searing winds, pestilence, and schemes, and you shall rest safe in the shadow of my wings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, is this bottle gonna start floating around you too?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Unfortunately, yes.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Great, we've got the Jinni, so let's go. We've spent too much time here already.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #I see a new path in the back, {NICKNAME}. Let's head that way!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Don't know, don't care! You coming?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jeht seems angry all of a sudden...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It is to be expected of a girl who has yet to become a mother, I fear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What does that even...?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hehe, come now, I do believe you are neither conservative nor craven. Even mortal peril holds an abominable attraction for you, does it not?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: If a reason you must have, an excuse you must claim, then say it is for a friend... Yes. "For a friend." What a lovely ring that has, wouldn't you say?

talks.objective: Leave through the gap caused by the collapse

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hmm... Now, where should I begin...?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the moonlight paints the stones white, and night wind blows chill, causing the tendrils of the campfire to snap and crackle... Amidst the calls of nocturnal birds winding across the distant sand dunes, the Jinni begins her tale...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Thousands of years have passed since the events told of in this tale. The desert had yet to become so desolate, and the oases spread out across the land like glittering jewels...\nIn those days, the Jinn walked the earth in great numbers, and they lived within the silver night wind and the flowing sands, in the ripples of the unknowable ocean, and in the pattering of the rainforest springs...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
We Jinn were not ordinary creatures, but we were the servants of the mistress of flowers.
We were untroubled by basic want, nor were we shackled by material thirst. It was "life" itself that greatly fascinated us...
The blooming and wilting of flowers, the gathering and scattering of birds — these were the things that held us in thrall.
Apart from that, only our "true names" could bind us.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: We were carefree so long as our mistress walked the earth, and we enjoyed her eternal paradise, her love, and her comfort...\nBut tragedy would come, and our paradise crumbled as the mistress departed... Our revelry turned to mourning, and all that was good and lovely was violently perverted in that anguish...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And so we gave Al-Ahmar our true names, and became his servants... For he promised to find us our eternal companion, our true master.\nDeluded hope and trust did we harbor in our hearts, and so forsook our freedom, accepting imprisonment within silver bottles and servitude to his realm...\nBut what was lost was forever lost, never again to return.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
But do not think that the Jinn were wanton servants.
Only a love bordering upon madness could make the Jinn give their "true names" willingly.
For it was their deep love for the mistress of flowers that drove them to embrace the desert from the first.
Yet, waking to face the tomfoolery of this barren world caused a surly Jinni to fall incurably in love with the shepherd...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Ah, you're awake...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A shepherd...?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Not you, no... Hah, but much like you, my master. You were... much like him — as he was once.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Well now, girl, does that make you jealous?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#No. It's just that I find this story quite familiar...}{F#Definitely not!}

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: #{M#That's because this story has happened before, and may yet happen again.}{F#Hah. She is quite transparent, my master. I once did have a daughter — my eyes are not deceived.}

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#Hmm...}{F#Hmph. Say whatever you like...}

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: *sigh* To the Jinn, "love" was a terrible chain, driving those who fell into its pit to make sacrifices, like the hyphae of a parasitic insect...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh boy, Liloupar's at it again with the scary analogies...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hehe, we Jinn do not have this tedious thing you humans call "shame," so we do not shy away from discussing love, or revealing one's all to a lover.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#*cough*!}{F#I'm suddenly glad that you're just a bottle now...}

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: But to the Jinn, this mad love could not be reconciled to betrayal. Or else, hatred and vengeance three times greater would be sure to follow.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: That was the root of the farce that ended Gurabad... Though that is a different tale.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Actually, now that you mention it, I'd like to ask a question... Did you really have no other goal in presenting your "true name"?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hmm? Hah, well, I suppose vigilance is wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Well, I do have something I seek. I wish to go to the Eternal Oasis, just as you do... There are things there that have been left unfinished.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And what may those be?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Forgive me, dear master, if I can only slowly tell you that tale as our journey proceeds. But the time for that has not yet come.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: But know this — it is good fortune that I should have met you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, since we've got the same goal, let's get along. How about a toast?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: And what shall you make this toast with? Me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft... Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Alright, weird-story-time's over! Let's talk about something more relaxing.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #By the way, {NICKNAME}, do you play cards?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, I don't.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Eh, alright then... I for one shall not complain if a more elegant pastime were chosen.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Oh, that so? Shame, then. Why don't we talk about some of the things we've seen, then?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You all speak about the interesting things you've heard about, as well as the hair-raising adventures you've been through. Some absolutely ridiculous hearsay is even mixed in...\nThe three of you raise toasts to old triumphs, laugh at ridiculous tales, and shed tears and lament the sad stories.\nAt the end, Azariq closes the proceedings with a joke, and he absolutely kills it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
#When the moon hangs highest, Azariq tells a rather coarse joke about a crocodile and a Sumpter Beast, which loses him his blanket-sharing privileges.
{M#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
She seems to have lived well amongst the Tanit since your last parting.}{F#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
A light scent of spices wafts from her, and it seems to you that all the stories she has to tell since your last parting seem tinged with this sadness.}

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The night flies by as you chat.\nAs the next morning comes, you are buried in each others' pillows, asleep by the extinguished flame.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #We're here! C'mon, let's find a place to sit and grab a bite, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Azariq, Jeht!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Haha, hardly that long! Good to see that you're all well. Jeht's really fond of you — we were just talking about you, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What did you talk about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is Jeht still angry?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Huh? Angry...?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Oh! She did mention a little disagreement you had, yes... But you know, she talks quite carelessly, but isn't actually good at expressing her feelings.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Still, you should reflect as well. Jeht's very concerned about your safety, so you should pay a bit more attention to her suggestions.

choices.text: Sorry, it was my mistake for leaving her out.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Sorry, it was my fault, really. I was... petty. Childish.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I knew how important Liloupar was to our mission, but I threw a tantrum anyway...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Liloupar says stuff weirdly, and she does use some pretty creepy analogies...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she looked out for us the whole way, so... Well, she's different from the people we've met so far for sure, but she doesn't seem like a bad person!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whatever the case... It'll be fine. {NICKNAME}'s important to you, isn't {F#she}{M#he}, Jeht?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#Of course. You're my best friends.}{F#Yeah, I mean, I've always seen you as my... best friend, but I'm just worried that... *sigh* Never mind.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeesh, you're so serious all of a sudden. Paimon doesn't know what to say at all...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ugh, there's no need to be so awkward! I won't get mad anyhow from now on, and you can count on that!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hahahaha! That's right, that's the spirit!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Ah, right! About the "Mother of the Jinn"... Is it with you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Azariq! Didn't Matriarch Babel tell you not to ask that willy-nilly?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: It's fine, Jeht! I mean, I guided you half the way, so I count as a "companion," don't I?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: A "companion," you say? Perhaps you speak too hastily.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Eh? The bottle's talking!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Such insolence! If you recognize me not, then your silence shall serve better!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Whoa, this is a pretty fierce one for sure... Is that the Mother of the Jinn, then?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I'd watch my tongue if I were you, desert-spawn.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: This is Azariq, one of my brothers here in the tribe.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hmph... Well, we could have chosen worse. This one is sturdy enough. A shame that he has too big a mouth, and too small a brain.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: *sigh* How is talking to her supposed to *not* end as an exercise in frustration?

choices.text: Reckon you just need to get used to it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, y'know, Jeht, you did find Benben pretty cute, didn't you? How about you just treat her like a Benben that talks! They both fly, don't they? Hehe.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Oh, it's fine! Sharp tongues are to be expected of the legendary Jinni... somewhat, I mean.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Whatever the case, she's on our side, isn't she? We'll be fine!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: On "your side"? Did I mishear you?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Apologies, but you shall not find me on the "side" of those who entreat my master while wearing two faces.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: #My master trusts you, and I trust {F#her}{M#his} reasoning for that. But I will be watching you, Azariq.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Heh... Well, I guess that's just what a Jinni's like...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: ...It's fine.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Ah, right. Did anything happen while we were separated? Just curious, I mean.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Same here. Did I miss anything?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, about that...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Jeht and Azariq about the ambush in the canyon, as well as Aderfi's departure from the camp...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: So, a traitor, along with accomplices from other tribes... They might be the same bunch I was tracking down previously. It's even possible that they're collaborating with dangerous outsiders like the Fatui.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hah, pretty good, Jeht. Made the best of some rather limited information on our foes there.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That's not too hard. I've been helping the Matriarch to track and... eliminate traitors, so their movements and patterns aren't that alien to me.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: My dad and I have also encountered those people who call themselves "Fatui" in the past, so they're no strangers to me either.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Still... I ran off in a huff without giving any thought to whether they would act... I'm sorry. That was my mistake.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, let's leave that aside for now. It wasn't even your fault...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: I'm with Paimon. Don't beat yourself up about this too much, Jeht. They seem to have been ordered specifically not to attack you — can't blame you for having lowered your guard there.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But as for Aderfi... Since he's fled in secret, it's beyond doubt that he's betrayed us. Those who violate the laws of hospitality and wield their blades against guests are unworthy of the Tanit's mercy.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #I'll capture him, {NICKNAME}, this I promise. He will not escape the Matriarch's judgment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hoho, Jeht's getting serious!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What? You make it sound like I've never been serious!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Haha! Becoming ever more the model of a tribeswoman, eh, Jeht?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What are you talking about? Aren't I one?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That's not what I mean. I'm just glad to see that you're so concerned about your friends.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: This is also a tribal matter, you know...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: True... Outsiders are becoming increasingly active in the desert, and as their interference increases, so too do changes of heart and thought.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: As Matriarch Babel's right and left hands, we should indeed be concerned about such things.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Exactly.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Ah, right. There's one more thing. It's Wenut season at the moment, so the tunnels they dig are starting to show up all around the desert.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Such areas are very dangerous, so we'll have to approach our adventure with more care and avoid them at all costs.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Wait. Just Wenut? Don't we always hunt them? They're no threat.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That's still no reason to drop your guard.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Sure, sure, I get it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's a Wenut?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, them? We hunt them every year, and then we collect their body fat and use that to make spices. We don't produce much, but it can be sold at a pretty price.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: So we don't really lack anything. We just need to control the Wenut hunting grounds, and our long-term prospects will stay good.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: City folk love these thick and pungent spices... But ask them about us desert folk, and they'll tell you a different story... We also need to hunt other animals, but the smell Wenut give off is too strong and will chase them off.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: As such, our spice workers can't take part in hunts, nor can they serve as assassins.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: As opposed to the scent of mature Wenut, their larvae give off a much gentler scent, which we often use for scent marks to prevent getting lost in caves or ruins...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Haha, you used that in the Gurabad ruins back there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... are they really that dangerous?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Not really...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: For you outsiders, perhaps?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But you needn't worry about that! We'll protect you!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Pfft...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? What's so funny?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It's nothing... Ah, the children of Apep, reduced to this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it, you haven't said anything in quite a while, Liloupar.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And I for my part was about to ask if you'd forgotten about someone. Well then. Would you like to hear a story?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, sure! As long as you have one to tell, anyway!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: *sigh* 'Tis a shame how long I've slumbered. I fear I am not current with the hot topics of the day, and am armed only with some ancient yarns. Will you mind, O master mine?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I'm all ears.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Don't worry, I've covered my ears!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon's covered h— Waaaait a minute. What are you covering your ears for?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The books say that the words of the Jinn have magic in them, and that their stories have the power to lay curses!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And they say also that behavior such as yours is impolite in the extreme! Do not interrupt me, little lady.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hmm... Now, where should I begin...?

dialogues.text: Wait but a moment, my master. Something is amiss up ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Do we really wanna pass this way, then?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...It matters not. This is the path we must take, in any case.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I am sure, my master, that you too are able to sense the wicked intent ahead... But if we might discover who it is that ambushes us, we might yet turn the tables on them.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Things may indeed be perilous ahead, but you, O master mine, are the one to whom I have entrusted my fate. I shall go forth with you, and we shall face any obstacle together.

response.text: #Just relax! {NICKNAME}'s super strong, and no matter what, {M#he'll}{F#she'll} still have Paimon, right?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hark, what did I say? Prepare yourself, master.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you guys... Aren't you Jeht's buddies?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, c'mon, don't scare Paimon here... Why aren't they replying?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Well, if this is what it comes to... Do not forget to leave one alive, master.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: We may follow that one's flight to find his allies and servants, and thus destroy their nest in one fell swoop.

dialogues.text: Welcome, guests of Tanit...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: You m—may d—do anything you please here in our camp...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Planting crops and f—feeding the fish. Sometimes, I also do some b—b—butchery. Crocodile skin and meat is v—very useful.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: We get clean spring water all year around h—here, so it's just right for raising crocodiles. Th—that's why we fenced this place up.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Crocodiles are easy to care for, and they can be harvested for lots of skins and meat. Unfortunately, f—fields are a d—different story...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You have fields around here?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: We do... but only for testing. Matriarch Babel invited some outsiders to c—c—come and provide us with Anahitian Blessing, and she got all these old books from the city...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: S—s—so we've tried our hand at farming according to the contents of these books.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: But the oases in the canyon are too narrow and lack nutrients. We need to find a way to f—fertilize the soil.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tell me about the Anahitian Blessing...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: The outsiders didn't want to reveal the fertilizer's composition. As such, we've had to rely on the people who provide it to f—fertilize the soil... which isn't good.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Th—that's why the Matriarch wants me to d—do some research here to r—reverse engineer our own Anahitian Blessing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I shan't disturb you any longer.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Th—that's alright. Please take some crocodile jerky, dear guest. It's just over there...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Hehe, yes. I—I take care of them. These are quite large and obedient...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: This one's c—c—called Sedim. Very fierce and strong, and skin's very vibrant. It'll make for a good satchel. And there's that one, Karam. It's small but plump. Rather gentle, too.

talks.objective: Track your foe by following the footprints

dialogues.speaker: Goods Invoice
dialogues.text: "May this be testimony that we have provided the material support required for this ambush and robbery. As a token of friendship, the gifts shall be sent via specially-arranged Sumpter Beast caravan..."

dialogues.speaker: Goods Invoice
dialogues.text: "The Tanit tribe sends respectful greetings to the Afiyah tribe. May peace follow you, and may spices fill your storehouses."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait just a second! The Tanit tribe...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's Jeht's tribe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that means... Ugh, were these guys hired by them?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Oho, so the desert people have learned to use books to keep records? Well, I suppose my awakening has given rise to fresh sights after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But what were they intending to do here, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Who knows? Most importantly, they were our foes.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Well, since we have found one part of a paper trail, we may as well search their encampment. There, I believe, we shall find more clues.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How do you know that's definitely the case?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Toads do not lay one egg at a time, and centipedes and scorpions huddle together in the damp shade.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, you and your creepy analogies again...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Whatever the case may be, we no longer need any of them in one piece. Let us proceed to the next encampment.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Hehe, so it's you... Youngster, I have heard that you and Jeht went into the accursed city. Ah, and you would like to know how I know this, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Hunters have falcons and hounds to be their eyes and ears, naturally. But young one, I must remind you that this word, the "curse," comes not out of thin air.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: A venom, the root of all tragedy, that drives all humans add, is hidden within a facade of flowing gold.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Perhaps it shall be so this time as well, that greedy prey shall fall into a trap, where they cannot be saved...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The night flies by amidst the card games and chats.\nAs the next morning comes, you are buried in each others' pillows, asleep by the extinguished flame.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Hah! Let's see what you'll have to say for yourself after {NICKNAME} thrashes you.

talks.objective: Return to the tribal settlement and report to Babel

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Allow me to dust you off. Jeht and Azariq are waiting for you as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We brought the object that you needed.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Jeht told me. Thank you both so much.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We were ambushed within the canyon on the way back.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were attacked by your people while on our way back! There were lots of people hiding in the canyon, waiting to intercept us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They were pretty scary, too! Do you know what all that was about?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: No, I haven't a clue how that happened.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Traitors and exiles turning to banditry on the roads is quite normal, but the canyons here should have a lot of tributaries... It seems that I've underestimated them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This has to do with Aderfi.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: ...What did you say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! We found this!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You give Aderfi's letter to Babel...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Aderfi... This is indeed his handwriting, and it is even signed in his hand. That he is a traitor is beyond doubt.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But... What if he's been set up?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Then he has still stained our honor with his name, and will accept his punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: However... *sigh* He left the camp some time ago, saying that he needed to go get some supplies from outside. I must apologize. I let my guard down.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: You can be sure that we will exile that traitor, however. He shall not be permitted back into the Tanit hunting grounds — save in chains.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Please rest assured, you two, that I will get to the bottom of this on behalf of our tribe. I will not allow such happenings to go unanswered.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: As for the "Mother of the Jinn"... Can I see her?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Honored Lady Liloupar, beloved servant of Nabu Malikata, founder of Gurabad, eternal prisoner of Ay-Khanoum, Babel of the mortal Tanit tribe seeks an audience with you.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: *yawn* Mmm... Hmm? What did you say? Were you calling for me? I don't quite remember all those names.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Yes. We ask only, Lady Liloupar, that you lead us to the Eternal Oasis, to set us on the path to meet with the slumbering queen.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: *yawn* So sleepy... My master, did you wake me to speak with this servant? *sigh* Why do you love consorting with these coarse folk so...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Well, then, Babel. Will you not dance? Amuse us, and we may yet grant you three wishes.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hmm? What? Oh, I'm so sorry, you're the mother of this tribe, riiight! Hahahaha!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: My apologies. I read the servility in your brows, and merely could not help but wish to see you dance and entertain us.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: I am merely your servant and will listen to all you have to say. I shall follow the dictates of the Queen of All Oases, Nabu Malikata's will with due trepidation, and them I will not defy.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hah! I shall not be so crude. Save your solicitations. I already have a master, and I do not intend to take on any servants either, so I fear your calculations have come to naught.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (...So Matriarch Babel can grovel too, huh...)

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: You have yet to see many things indeed!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: My master, you hold my true name, I shall do what you, and only you, desire.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: The decision shall be yours. I will not speak another word to these foul desert dwellers.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: "Master"... Your "master"...?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: #Why, yes indeed, and it is this noble {M#prince}{F#princess} you see before you. Now, now, you need not kneel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (C'mon, say something, why don't you!? Just look at her face!)

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: #I understand. In that case... Will you help us, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I will help you find the Eternal Oasis.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: If that is your choice, then I gladly obey.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Well then, I shall lend my aid. A pleasure to work with you, desert woman!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: But a word to the wise: nothing save death can break a contract forged by "true names."

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And I will be watching you on my master's account... Do not think for a moment that you may wield me.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: ...I understand.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And it is good that you do, dweller of the sands. Now then, do not disturb my rest.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: So, you have forged a contract with her, then...?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Yes, I understand. You have done well.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Jinn are arrogant, unfettered creatures, and yet you have managed to bind her. You have surpassed my expectations indeed...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: But that is well. Our path to the Eternal Oasis has been made smoother.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: #So please, {NICKNAME}, if I may ask something of you... Keep Liloupar loyal at all costs...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: You have my thanks.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Ah, Jeht and Azariq have returned. You youngsters catch up for now. I'll have to ask for your pardon, I need some time to organize the information you have gathered...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ms. Babel sure is busy, huh?

choices.text: To do otherwise would be looking for trouble.
I did it to open the way.
I came here to help fulfill Jeht's wish.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #We're here! C'mon, let's find a place to sit and grab a bite, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Azariq, Jeht!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Haha, hardly that long! Good to see that you're all well. Jeht's really fond of you — we were just talking about you, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What did you talk about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is Jeht still angry?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Huh? Angry...?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Oh! She did mention a little disagreement you had, yes... But you know, she talks quite carelessly, but isn't actually good at expressing her feelings.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Still, you should reflect as well. Jeht's very concerned about your safety, so you should pay a bit more attention to her suggestions.

choices.text: Sorry, it was my mistake for leaving her out.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Sorry, it was my fault, really. I was... petty. Childish.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I knew how important Liloupar was to our mission, but I threw a tantrum anyway...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Liloupar says stuff weirdly, and she does use some pretty creepy analogies...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she looked out for us the whole way, so... Well, she's different from the people we've met so far for sure, but she doesn't seem like a bad person!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whatever the case... It'll be fine. {NICKNAME}'s important to you, isn't {F#she}{M#he}, Jeht?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#Of course. You're my best friends.}{F#Yeah, I mean, I've always seen you as my... best friend, but I'm just worried that... *sigh* Never mind.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeesh, you're so serious all of a sudden. Paimon doesn't know what to say at all...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ugh, there's no need to be so awkward! I won't get mad anyhow from now on, and you can count on that!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hahahaha! That's right, that's the spirit!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Ah, right! About the "Mother of the Jinn"... Is it with you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Azariq! Didn't Matriarch Babel tell you not to ask that willy-nilly?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: It's fine, Jeht! I mean, I guided you half the way, so I count as a "companion," don't I?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: A "companion," you say? Perhaps you speak too hastily.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Eh? The bottle's talking!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Such insolence! If you recognize me not, then your silence shall serve better!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Whoa, this is a pretty fierce one for sure... Is that the Mother of the Jinn, then?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I'd watch my tongue if I were you, desert-spawn.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: This is Azariq, one of my brothers here in the tribe.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hmph... Well, we could have chosen worse. This one is sturdy enough. A shame that he has too big a mouth, and too small a brain.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: *sigh* How is talking to her supposed to *not* end as an exercise in frustration?

choices.text: Reckon you just need to get used to it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, y'know, Jeht, you did find Benben pretty cute, didn't you? How about you just treat her like a Benben that talks! They both fly, don't they? Hehe.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Oh, it's fine! Sharp tongues are to be expected of the legendary Jinni... somewhat, I mean.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Whatever the case, she's on our side, isn't she? We'll be fine!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: On "your side"? Did I mishear you?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Apologies, but you shall not find me on the "side" of those who entreat my master while wearing two faces.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: #My master trusts you, and I trust {F#her}{M#his} reasoning for that. But I will be watching you, Azariq.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Heh... Well, I guess that's just what a Jinni's like...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: ...It's fine.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Ah, right. Did anything happen while we were separated? Just curious, I mean.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Same here. Did I miss anything?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, about that...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Jeht and Azariq about the ambush in the canyon, as well as Aderfi's departure from the camp...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: So, a traitor, along with accomplices from other tribes... They might be the same bunch I was tracking down previously. It's even possible that they're collaborating with dangerous outsiders like the Fatui.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hah, pretty good, Jeht. Made the best of some rather limited information on our foes there.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That's not too hard. I've been helping the Matriarch to track and... eliminate traitors, so their movements and patterns aren't that alien to me.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: My dad and I have also encountered those people who call themselves "Fatui" in the past, so they're no strangers to me either.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Still... I ran off in a huff without giving any thought to whether they would act... I'm sorry. That was my mistake.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, let's leave that aside for now. It wasn't even your fault...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: I'm with Paimon. Don't beat yourself up about this too much, Jeht. They seem to have been ordered specifically not to attack you — can't blame you for having lowered your guard there.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But as for Aderfi... Since he's fled in secret, it's beyond doubt that he's betrayed us. Those who violate the laws of hospitality and wield their blades against guests are unworthy of the Tanit's mercy.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #I'll capture him, {NICKNAME}, this I promise. He will not escape the Matriarch's judgment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hoho, Jeht's getting serious!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What? You make it sound like I've never been serious!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Haha! Becoming ever more the model of a tribeswoman, eh, Jeht?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What are you talking about? Aren't I one?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That's not what I mean. I'm just glad to see that you're so concerned about your friends.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: This is also a tribal matter, you know...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: True... Outsiders are becoming increasingly active in the desert, and as their interference increases, so too do changes of heart and thought.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: As Matriarch Babel's right and left hands, we should indeed be concerned about such things.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Exactly.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Ah, right. There's one more thing. It's Wenut season at the moment, so the tunnels they dig are starting to show up all around the desert.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Such areas are very dangerous, so we'll have to approach our adventure with more care and avoid them at all costs.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Wait. Just Wenut? Don't we always hunt them? They're no threat.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That's still no reason to drop your guard.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Sure, sure, I get it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's a Wenut?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, them? We hunt them every year, and then we collect their body fat and use that to make spices. We don't produce much, but it can be sold at a pretty price.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: So we don't really lack anything. We just need to control the Wenut hunting grounds, and our long-term prospects will stay good.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: City folk love these thick and pungent spices... But ask them about us desert folk, and they'll tell you a different story... We also need to hunt other animals, but the smell Wenut give off is too strong and will chase them off.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: As such, our spice workers can't take part in hunts, nor can they serve as assassins.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: As opposed to the scent of mature Wenut, their larvae give off a much gentler scent, which we often use for scent marks to prevent getting lost in caves or ruins...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Haha, you used that in the Gurabad ruins back there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... are they really that dangerous?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Not really...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: For you outsiders, perhaps?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But you needn't worry about that! We'll protect you!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Pfft...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? What's so funny?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It's nothing... Ah, the children of Apep, reduced to this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it, you haven't said anything in quite a while, Liloupar.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And I for my part was about to ask if you'd forgotten about someone. Well then. Would you like to hear a story?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, sure! As long as you have one to tell, anyway!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: *sigh* 'Tis a shame how long I've slumbered. I fear I am not current with the hot topics of the day, and am armed only with some ancient yarns. Will you mind, O master mine?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I'm all ears.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Don't worry, I've covered my ears!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon's covered h— Waaaait a minute. What are you covering your ears for?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The books say that the words of the Jinn have magic in them, and that their stories have the power to lay curses!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And they say also that behavior such as yours is impolite in the extreme! Do not interrupt me, little lady.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #What's the matter, {NICKNAME}? Don't just stand there, let's play some cards. Don't worry! I swear I won't mock you — not even if you're absolutely terrible.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Come on, let's play a round.

choices.text: Oh, I'm not going to lose...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Not liking camping out here in the desert, I take it? Haha, oh well... Why don't we tell some stories instead?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You all speak about the interesting things you've heard about, as well as the hair-raising adventures you've been through. Some absolutely ridiculous hearsay is even mixed in...\nThe three of you raise toasts to old triumphs, laugh at ridiculous tales, and shed tears and lament the sad stories.\nAt the end, Azariq closes the proceedings with a joke, and he absolutely kills it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text:
#When the moon hangs highest, Azariq tells a rather coarse joke about a crocodile and a Sumpter Beast, which loses him his blanket-sharing privileges.
{M#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
She seems to have lived well amongst the Tanit since your last parting.}{F#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
A light scent of spices wafts from her, and it seems to you that all the stories she has to tell since your last parting seem tinged with this sadness.}

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The night flies by as you chat.\nAs the next morning comes, you are buried in each others' pillows, asleep by the extinguished flame.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Alright! That's one device done and dusted.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hmm? The door we came through has been sealed. We're going to have to find another way through.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: It's said that the destruction of the city was not a deed done from without, but that it fell to revolt from within. That certainly lines up with what we've seen...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Most of the damage was done to the interior. Perhaps it was a slave revolt? Or a civil war between priests?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It could also be the work of long years of disrepair or Wenut activity, right?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Wenut...? I doubt that much at least. Wenut don't dare to touch these ruins, and if the elders are to be believed, that's because this city is "ill-fated."

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Alright, enough ghost stories for now. Let's keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Phew, we're back at the temple!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Well, next up, let's get the issue of the large device at the center squared away, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... How are you all not dizzy from all this looping around?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Look, there's sand flowing down from the cracks. It seems that some place deeper within the ruins is shaking!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Yes, I sense it too.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: These empty hallways all eventually lead back to the same center. How did the people who worshiped the gods here live...?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Alright, little wildcat. Rather than caring about how now-dead people lived, you should have a care for how you might yet die.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, I have a care for how you might, sure!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Oh? But let me guess — you can't bear to tell me?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You two really do get along nicely...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: The blood of outsiders does not mix with that of the tribe, so in many things, I tend to represent something of an "exception"...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: And since I've already been to lots of places that are "bad luck," they were fine with sending me to explore this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Aren't they just ostracizing you!?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, no... The tribe's just like that. They treat me very well, but I have an outsider's blood. That's all there is to it.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It's just like the book says... "Under the influence of the Jinn, though the land was as a barren desert, it would grow into a verdant oasis..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look at that. Isn't there something shiny under that big tree? Could that be the Jinni we're looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Careful, Paimon! We're not sure if this place is safe yet!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
